tool_summary: RHEL/CentOS/older Fedora's package manager. Installs, upgrades, and removes system packages, typically requiring root, and runs arbitrary %post/%postun scriptlets at install/remove time.
platform_notes: yum is specific to RHEL/CentOS and older Fedora releases; dnf has superseded it on newer systems but yum remains in wide use.

rules.description: The --nogpgcheck flag disables GPG signature verification for the packages being installed, removing the primary protection against tampered packages.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its install-time scriptlets may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The addrepo/config-manager --add-repo subcommands add a third-party repository as a trusted package source. An untrusted or unfamiliar repository is a common supply-chain attack vector.
rules.notes: yum-config-manager is typically a separate binary/wrapper; this rule covers only the case where repo addition is invoked via `yum addrepo` directly (if supported by the installed yum plugin set). yum-config-manager itself would need its own ruleset file to be assessed under its own name.

rules.description: Installs a package, running arbitrary %post scriptlets with root privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but install-time scriptlets may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Manages system packages. Read-only subcommands (list, info, search) do not alter system state.
